Usage: belz cache --env <name> [flags] <uuid...>
       belz cache --env <name> --all --yes [--type <TYPE>]
       belz cache prune-local [--yes]

Invalidate server-side cache entries on an environment, or clean up stale
local cache artifacts under ~/.belz/cache.

Invalidating is a remote write, so it requires an explicit --env (the default
env is never used). prune-local touches local files only and needs no --env.

Server-side invalidate (default subcommand): every call is POSTed to BOTH
/rest/api/cache/invalidate and /rest/api/automations/cache/invalidate with
body {"uuids":[...],"type":"<TYPE>"}; it succeeds if any route returns 2xx,
and each route's result is reported.

An invalidate with no UUIDs flushes the ENTIRE cache of that type for the whole
organisation, so it is refused unless both --all and --yes are passed.

Subcommands:
  prune-local         Remove stale LOCAL cache artifacts left from before caches
                      became env-scoped: flat <namespace>/<key>.json files
                      (current layout is <namespace>/<env>/<key>.json) and
                      abandoned .refresh/*.lock files older than 10 minutes.
                      Local filesystem only — no network request, not
                      environment-specific. Default is a dry run; pass --yes
                      to actually delete.
    --yes, -y         Delete the listed files instead of only listing them.

Args:
  <uuid...>           One or more cache entry UUIDs (e.g. method/chain UUIDs).
                      Each must be 32 hex characters (or dashed UUID form);
                      anything else (e.g. a mistyped subcommand) → INVALID_UUID.

Flags:
  --type <TYPE>       Cache type to invalidate. (default: AUTOMATION)
  --all               Flush every entry of --type (org-wide). Requires --yes.
  --yes, -y           Confirm an --all flush, or (with prune-local) confirm deletion.
  --help, -h          Show this help message.

Global Flags:
  --env <name>        Environment to operate on. Required for invalidation.
                      Also accepts --env=<name> or -e <name>.
  --llm               Output structured JSON envelope for scripting/LLM use.
  -v, --verbose       Verbose request logging.

Examples:
  # Invalidate three automation cache entries on nsm-dev
  belz cache --env nsm-dev 44014c3707d6b6d8ae848839a1c8d1e7 47425344e088690ff89aa8f1e092c867 4a1d686b87f93b1519f2b61393d4ed7a

  # Two entries on nsm-qa
  belz cache --env nsm-qa <uuid> <uuid>

  # Wipe the entire AUTOMATION cache on nsm-uat (org-wide; use with care)
  belz cache --env nsm-uat --all --yes

  # Invalidate by a non-default type
  belz cache --env nsm-dev --type PAGE <uuid>

  # See what local cache cleanup would remove (dry run)
  belz cache prune-local

  # Actually delete stale local cache artifacts
  belz cache prune-local --yes
